newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech c.bank puts further limits on Lombard access.
newsitem.headline: Czech c.bank puts further limits on Lombard access.

text.p: The Czech central bank (CNB) on Wednesday said it had begun to implement further limits on banks's access to the CNB's last resort lending facility, the Lombard rate.
"Today access to the Lombard facility will be further limited as compared to Tuesday," CNB bank board member Ludek Niedermeyer told Reuters.
He did not elaborate on the limits set, but on Tuesday the central bank limited access to the Lombard facility by banks to a portion of the capital.
"We will react in order to stabilise the currency, so we are willing to cut it (access) to...zero," he said.

Last Friday the CNB raised the Lombard rate from 14 percent to 50 percent in a move aimed against speculative selling of the crown, once regarded as the most stable currency in post-communist central Europe.
Niedermeyer said the central bank restriction applied equally to all foreign and Czech banks with a licence to operate in the country.

But he added that the policy toward bank branches in the Czech Republic -- which have argued against the move since they are severely limited because their capital is virtually non-existent locally -- had not changed.
"They (branches) were very unhappy but we will not change our policy," he said.
